proof.criterion: Review round 1's claim finding, which this round fixed: the label walk runs inside the claim's own transaction, so its failure must cost a sentence of guidance and never the claim, and the answer must omit the field rather than state that Legion does not own the status.
proof.surface: A third lane of the same rig: port 18879, the same branch binary, against database dispatch_t_boom whose search_path names public before pg_catalog and whose public.lower(text) raises for exactly one value, 'tester-boom', and delegates to pg_catalog.lower for every other. An issue whose first label is 'tester-boom' therefore makes `select … where lower(label) = 'legion'` raise inside the claim's transaction, and nothing else in the server changes. The issue also carries legion, so a healthy walk would answer true: today's wording there can only be the omitted field.
proof.command: bash /legion/scratch/harness/boom.sh — dispatch claim and --release on the forced-failure issue, dispatch read of it, a raw POST /api/v1/issues/<KEY>/claim for the wire shape, a dispatch comment for the advice path, and the same calls on a control issue labelled legion alone on the same server.
proof.observed: 19 assertions, 0 failures (/legion/scratch/harness/boom.log). The claim succeeded ('claimed by you since …'), dispatch read showed the issue really held it, and both the claim and the release printed today's wording and never the Legion sentence. On the wire the answer carried the issue and its claim with legion_managed_status absent, not false. The server logged 'dispatch: claim legion_managed_status omitted' once per call. On the write-advice path the same failure drops the whole advice, as every advice query failure has always done ('dispatch: write advice omitted … query=legion_managed_status'), and the comment itself still posted.
proof.negativeControl: The control issue on the same server, labelled legion alone so the walk never reaches 'tester-boom', answered legion_managed_status=true on the wire, named Legion as the mover, and dropped its triage line with legion_managed_status=true recorded — so the injection is targeted at the walk and the lane is not simply broken. Before the fix this same failure would have discarded the claim: the deferred rollback ran on the claim's own transaction.

breakAttempts: Round 1's break attempts were all re-run at this head after the helpers moved to issue_parent.go: the client memo stays unmarked while the line is suppressed, so the same session is told as soon as another session takes the label off, and a session already told is not told twice; a person's write keeps the line and resolves no field; a human event resets the caller's own count; an issue past triage resolves the field not at all; the walk is live, so a label put on the parent afterwards flips the child; the deepest legal descendant (32 links, the parentDepthCap boundary) still resolves true and a 33rd link is refused; a near-miss label (legionary) keeps today's wording; the inner-ref refusal for doc-edit names the issue alone; two sessions posting at the same instant each count only their own.

New this round: the claim path's walk forced to fail in the database (above). Also checked that the release by the holder keeps today's wording there, that the raw answer omits the field rather than carrying false, and that the failure is logged once per call rather than retried.

The advice path's behaviour under the same failure is recorded rather than filed: a failing legion_managed_status query drops the write's whole advice, the cadence and open-ask lines included, because computeWriteAdvice has always been all-or-nothing per write (write_advice.go returns nil on any adviceQueryError). The write itself still lands. That is the pre-existing contract this change joined, not a regression, and it is the reason this handoff's A3 proof reads recorded advice rather than an absent line.
testsJudged: Review round 1's two gaps are closed: write_advice_test.go and issue_claim_test.go each gained a grandchild row and a LEGION row, so a refactor of legionManagedStatusSQL to a single parent lookup, or to a two-spelling match, now fails the suite. TestClaimSurvivesAFailingLegionLabelWalk pins this round's fix by swapping the package-level SQL var for a statement Postgres refuses, and asserts the claim is in the answer, that the field is omitted from the raw body, and that a reader sees the claim on the issue — which is what my forced-failure lane drove end to end through the CLI. The vacuous TestCreateAskOnIssueKeepsSuggestionsWhenWriteAdviceFails now opens both asks as a session, the only actor that reaches computeWriteAdvice, so the armed hook fires again. I found no way to break the changed surface that no test would catch, so no red test was written this round.
